svg.text: The verb: keep the balance
Take the same off both pans; the altar takes a move only when it is done to both. Free the crystal and it shows its weight
1. Lift a gem
it glows; the altar waits for its twin
(the twins glow on the other pan)
2. Lift its twin
the same on both pans: both float off
with a chime, the chains glow green
3. Again, and again
the crystal stands alone; nothing waits
4. Free!
the chains snap, the Glimmer wakes; the
gems count: one, two, three, four
Not fair: one pan only
A gem taken from the crystal's pan alone, then the crystal tapped:
the chains rattle softly, the gem springs back, nothing changes.
Hoot: "The altar wants fair moves. The same on both pans!"
Carrying a gem across to the other pan is refused the same way.
Why the beam is held
A free-swinging beam would show which pan is heavier,
and a child could find the crystal by weighing it
(lift things off until it looks level): no algebra.
The frozen crystal's chains hold the beam level, so
the only way to free it is to keep the balance.
